title: Choose a project with less searching
summary: People open the project picker many times a day. Today it starts empty, so they type the same names again and again. This proposal shows recent projects first and gives each state a clear message and a next step.
recommendation: Show recent projects before the first search. Keep the search field available in every state. Give a failed request a Retry button that keeps the search text.
scope: This proposal covers the layout and the messages of the picker. It does not change which projects a person can open, and it does not change search ranking.

terms.empty state: What the picker shows when a search finds no projects. It tells the person what happened and what to try next.
terms.recent projects: The last five projects that this person opened on this device, newest first.

approval.covers: Build the four picker states in the web app, with one test for each state. The agent opens one pull request.

sections.title: The four picker states
sections.summary: Each preview is a static HTML copy of the proposed state. It is not the running product.

blocks.title: Recent projects stay visible
blocks.body: The picker opens with recent projects. The selected row has a check mark and a border, so the selection does not depend on color alone.

blocks.title: Explain an empty search
blocks.body: The empty state repeats the search text and offers to clear it.

blocks.title: Show that results are loading
blocks.body: The search field stays active while the list loads. Screen readers hear that the list is loading.

blocks.title: Give a failed request a next step
blocks.body: The message says that the request failed, keeps the search text, and offers Retry.

blocks.title: What does the picker show before the first search?
blocks.body: Most people open one of a few projects. A list of recent projects saves typing for them. A search-only picker is simpler but makes every person type.

options.label: Recent projects
options.benefit: Most people pick a project with one click.
options.cost: The picker must store a short list on each device.

options.label: Search field only
options.benefit: Nothing to store, and the first view is very simple.
options.cost: People type a name every time.

blocks.title: How does a failed request recover?

options.label: A Retry button
options.benefit: The person controls when to try again, and the message stays until it works.
options.cost: One more click after a short network problem.

options.label: Retry by itself after 3 seconds
options.benefit: Short network problems fix themselves without a click.
options.cost: The list can change while the person reads it.

blocks.title: Do projects that a person cannot open appear in the list?
blocks.body: The permission service already decides who can open a project. The picker only needs to know whether to hide those projects or show them as locked.
blocks.placeholder: For example: hide them, or show them with a lock and the name of the owner
